features.description: A maintainer can verify one pinned Codex source, schema, license, and build identity before any candidate runtime is allowed to start.
steps: Run the Codex Harness supply-chain contract against the committed lock and generated source receipt.
Observe exact upstream/fork/schema/toolchain/license matches and rejection of unlocked or mismatched artifacts.

features.description: A session can create, append, flush, resume, and cursor-read a durable Codex Thread while V1 clients receive an ordered compatibility stream.
steps: Create a Thread, append concurrent Items, restart the Runtime, and resume from PostgreSQL.
Observe gap-free sequence order, idempotent replay, tenant isolation, and the expected assistant-turn-contract/v1 projection.

features.description: A pure-text Turn runs through Codex Harness and the private model-only Gateway path without invoking the Python AgentLoop.
steps: Start a candidate Turn with a signed immutable runtime snapshot and stream a real model response.
Observe one billed model path, requested/effective reasoning metadata, visible TTFT, resumable history, and zero provider 400 responses.

features.description: The Codex kernel discovers and uses tenant-scoped Knowledge, tools, MCP, skills, citations, and artifacts without prompt keyword routing.
steps: Run representative Knowledge, research, coding, attachment, and office-read scenarios through the candidate.
Observe capability-driven discovery, compact structured results, artifact/citation Items, and no cross-tenant reuse.

features.description: Write and long-running tools remain approval-gated, idempotent, stop-safe, and recoverable under the Codex lifecycle.
steps: Interrupt before dispatch, during read-only work, after unknown write dispatch, and while approval is pending.
Observe one result per call, side_effect_unknown for uncertain writes, no blind retry, durable approval recovery, and no orphan process.

features.description: A legacy quiescent session imports exactly once and real product journeys pass in Docker before stable session canary promotion.
steps: Resume legacy sessions and execute the full authenticated browser and Agent Eval matrix on the Codex candidate.
Observe atomic import receipts, stable kernel ownership, successful rollback rehearsal, healthy services, and every canary quality/performance gate.

features.description: All surfaces consume the V2 Thread/Turn/Item contract and the Python loop can be removed without losing compatibility or rollback evidence.
steps: Run Web and SDK journeys through V2 after a full canary window and confirm zero production calls to the legacy loop.
Observe native event fidelity, a passing V1 deprecation window, rollback rehearsal, and deletion gates before removing legacy orchestration.
